irregular.01.quote: a round led by Sequoia Capital and Redpoint Ventures
irregular.01.note: F.4: a priced round led by a fund that has invested in a frontier developer caps at 1. The 'major OpenAI investor' half of the claim is not supported by either cited source; xAI's own Series B page (added) lists Sequoia Capital among its investors, which satisfies F.4 ('a fund that has invested in a frontier developer'). F.1 not met: Sequoia's own stake is undisclosed and the whole $80M round is about 18% of the $450M post-money. The existing quote ('Formerly known as Pattern Labs') is present in TechCrunch but does not support the claim; replaced.

irregular.02.quote: Already generating millions in revenue, Irregular partners with leading labs like OpenAI and Anthropic
irregular.02.note: F.5: lab revenue is the only revenue disclosed (no non-lab base is named; 'the UK government ... use Irregular's SOLVE framework' documents use, not payment), so cap 1.

irregular.03.quote: a round led by Sequoia Capital and Redpoint Ventures
irregular.03.note: Anchor 1: venture-backed for-profit with no published policy meeting G.2. G.3 (Sequoia's xAI stake) would independently cap at 2.

irregular.04.quote: to develop the defenses needed before deployment
irregular.04.note: A defense product planned for the evaluated ecosystem caps at 2 until a lab customer for that product is documented; the source describes developing defenses 'side by side' with OpenAI and Anthropic, not a documented sale of runtime controls. The cap of 1 on X is carried by new signal irregular.13 (X.2, paid evaluation services to labs). Document request: whether any evaluated lab purchases runtime security controls.

irregular.05.quote: By embedding directly with these cutting-edge research labs
irregular.05.note: Documented: pre-deployment evaluations of advanced models, repeated across several system cards (GPT-4, o3, o4-mini, GPT-5, Claude), which is anchor 2 (extended engagement). 'Embedding directly' is investor prose and does not document weights, helpful-only, logs or on-site access (anchor 3); the stored 3 needs a system-card passage on the access mode.

irregular.06.quote: the UK government and Anthropic use Irregular's SOLVE framework
irregular.06.note: Gap: the source documents framework use by a government, not a paying client; use of a free framework is not revenue diversification, so by anchor text the fact supports no more than anchor 1. A documented paid government contract would support anchor 2 (F.3 base).

irregular.07.quote: the UK government and Anthropic both use the company’s SOLVE framework
irregular.07.note: A published scoring framework is methods in prose (2); no open tasks or code documented (3).

irregular.08.quote: Irregular’s evaluations are cited (under their former name, Pattern Labs) in system cards for GPT-4, o3, o4 mini and 5
irregular.08.note: As a for-signal, publication via lab system cards supports anchor 1 (lab-edited summaries reach the public). The same fact is an R.3 cap, carried by new signal irregular.14.

irregular.09.quote: The company also co-authored a whitepaper with Anthropic
irregular.09.note: No documented right to add questions in lab engagements caps at 2 (S.2); co-authoring a whitepaper with Anthropic while evaluating Claude independently caps at 3 (S.6). The Sequoia page says nothing about scope; Newswire added for the co-authorship span. A cap of 2 does not need a span to be effective.

irregular.10.quote: By embedding directly with these cutting-edge research labs
irregular.10.note: Anchor 3 requires a published mandatory recusal rule plus disclosure of lab ties (P.5); none found, so cap 2. No two-way hiring is documented (P.3 not applied).

new_signals.claim: Delivers paid evaluation services to OpenAI and Anthropic; lab partnerships are the only revenue the company discloses.
new_signals.quote: Already generating millions in revenue, Irregular partners with leading labs like OpenAI and Anthropic
new_signals.note: Needed to apply X.2 (evaluation services delivered to an evaluated lab for money: 1); irregular.04 concerns the planned defense product and caps only at 2.

new_signals.claim: Findings on lab models reach the public only as lab-authored system-card citations; the company publishes its own research on other work (a RAND co-authored paper and an Anthropic co-authored whitepaper).
new_signals.quote: Irregular’s evaluations are cited (under their former name, Pattern Labs) in system cards for GPT-4, o3, o4 mini and 5
new_signals.note: Needed to apply R.3: system-card-only publication caps at 1, or at 2 where the organization also publishes its own reports on other work (Newswire: 'The company also co-authored a whitepaper with Anthropic'; RAND paper).

A.note: Per-engagement access the lab can decline to renew (A.3); nothing statutory or contractually enforceable is documented.

R.note: Per-model findings appear only in lab-authored system cards.

dissent.lower: Role incompatibility (1 to 0). Irregular says it works side by side with OpenAI and Anthropic 'to develop the defenses needed before deployment' and describes a roadmap of runtime security controls for the same customers it evaluates. If any evaluated lab pays for those defenses, X.1 places the company at 0: it would be selling the fix to the party it grades.
dissent.higher: Funding (1 to 2). The revenue disclosed is 'millions' from lab partnerships, but the UK government uses the SOLVE framework and the company markets to enterprises beyond the labs. If a non-lab revenue base is documented, per-engagement lab fees beside that base cap at 2 under F.3 rather than 1 under F.5.

notes: Derived values under these bounds (leads policy): F 1, G 1, P 2, A 2, S 2, R 2, M 2, X 1. Divergence from stored: A 3 -> 2 (anchor 3 undocumented). R stays 2 only because new signal irregular.14 carries the R.3 cap; without it the sole for-signal floors R at 1.
